🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Incubus frontman Brandon Boyd is making his feature-film scoring debut. Boyd is co-composing the score for the indie sci-fi thriller Unknown Company alongside Gregory Rogove, director Vincent Talenti announced on Instagram on Friday, November 6, 2026.

“Excited to announce @brandonboyd is making his feature film scoring debut alongside @gregoryrogove on UNKNOWN COMPANY,” Talenti wrote. “It was a blast collaborating on this haunting, atmospheric score.”

The film is a World War II-set sci-fi thriller now in post-production. Directed by Talenti and written by Gavin Hignight, it follows a small unit of American soldiers sent behind enemy lines in the final days of World War II to recover the wreckage of an unidentified object — a mission that becomes a confrontation with something beyond their understanding.

Ross Marquand leads the cast, with Hugh Scott, Zak Steiner, Mace Coronel, Kevin Brooks, Sarah Hay and Nolan North. Talenti produced the film with Eva Ceja, Dylan Palley and Matt Ryan. Bret Rudnick is executive producer.

Boyd said he had a great time working on the score with his longtime friend Rogove. “I had such a great time doing this film score with my ol' pal Greg Rogove,” he told The Hollywood Reporter. “The film is creepy, beautiful and dark and we composed music that meets the film there.”

Boyd is best known as the lead singer of Incubus, the band behind hits including “Drive,” “Wish You Were Here” and “Pardon Me,” and he has also released solo albums. He is a longtime fan of horror and science fiction.

No release date for Unknown Company has been announced.

Sources: The Hollywood Reporter, via Vincent Talenti on Instagram; KZK101. Images: The Hollywood Reporter, via Vincent Talenti on Instagram (@vincenttalenti).
